identification.summary: TA570 is a Proofpoint-designated cybercrime threat actor, described as one of the most active Qbot (Qakbot) malware affiliates and tracked by Proofpoint since 2018 [S4]. It distributes Qakbot by thread-hijacked email, and its Qakbot builds carry the botnet tag 'obama' (for example obama186, obama264), which is why it is nicknamed the 'presidents' affiliate [S3][S4][S7].
identification.notes: Malpedia lists DEV-0450 as a synonym; this record treats it as a Microsoft in-development designation, and no Microsoft primary document was opened to confirm the mapping [S4]. Sources gathered do not describe TA577 and should not be applied to TA570 [S7].

attribution.confidence: Proofpoint characterizes TA570 as a cybercrime threat actor, not a state actor [S4]. No source gathered attributes it to a nation or names individuals. The country value RU in the imported record is unsupported by the sources gathered.
attribution.basis: Proofpoint tracking since 2018, and Proofpoint observation of the June 2022 Follina campaign as reported by The Record, SANS ISC and Proofpoint's newsroom summary [S1][S3][S4].

objectives: As a Qbot affiliate it distributes Qbot to victim networks; Qakbot has been closely associated with ransomware attacks, per Krebs reporting on the 2023 takedown [S5]. TA570's own monetization path is not stated in the sources gathered.

targeting.notes: No source gathered describes TA570 victim sectors or regions; the email campaigns are described as thread hijacking of existing conversations, which is opportunistic mass targeting .

capabilities.summary: Thread-hijacked email carrying an HTML attachment that builds a ZIP via HTML smuggling; the archive held a shortcut (LNK), a hidden Qakbot DLL executed with rundll32.exe, and a Word document [S3]. In June 2022 it added the Follina flaw (CVE-2022-30190, an unpatched Windows MSDT issue at that time) through a Word document that loaded HTML containing PowerShell to download and run Qbot; Proofpoint suggested the group may have been A/B testing the two delivery methods [S1].

campaigns.name: Follina (CVE-2022-30190) Qbot campaign
campaigns.summary: TA570 sent thread-hijacked emails with HTML attachments dropping a ZIP with a Word document exploiting Follina, plus a LNK and DLL path to run Qbot (obama186); Proofpoint suggested A/B testing.

campaigns.name: obama264 Qakbot infection
campaigns.summary: A malware-traffic-analysis post records an obama264 Qakbot infection and notes TA570 still pushing Qakbot with the 'obama' tag at that time.

campaigns.name: Qakbot botnet takedown (Operation Duck Hunt)
campaigns.summary: FBI-led operation announced seizure of Qakbot infrastructure and an uninstall mechanism for infected hosts; reporting gathered did not name TA570.

diamond.adversary: Proofpoint-tracked cybercrime Qbot affiliate; no personas or nationality sourced [S4].
diamond.capability: Thread-hijacking email, HTML smuggling, LNK/DLL execution, Follina exploitation, Qakbot malware [S1][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Qakbot botnet infrastructure under the 'obama' tag; specific C2 and delivery hosts not gathered [S7].
diamond.victim: Recipients of hijacked email threads; sectors not sourced .
diamond.technology: Windows endpoints with Office and MSDT, mail systems exposing user threads, and unpatched software at the time of the Follina disclosure [S1].

gaps: Proofpoint's primary TA570 reporting (2021) was not opened; only search-result summaries were used [S1][S3].
Microsoft's DEV-0450 designation and its RaaS blog (2022-05-09) were not verified; DEV-0450 comes from Malpedia [S4].
TA570 activity after the August 2023 takedown is not documented in sources gathered; whether it stopped, switched loaders or returned is unknown.
Country of origin, personnel, ransomware partners, victims and sectors are not sourced.
Relationship to TA577 and other Qbot affiliates is not sourced.
Primary DOJ/FBI Duck Hunt documents were not opened; coverage was via press [S5].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is user mailboxes and Windows endpoints with Office, because delivery relies on hijacked email threads and document or shortcut execution [S3]. STEP 2: The actor is a commodity affiliate, so threat is broad rather than targeted at DoD; the adversary has demonstrated fast adoption of a fresh zero-day (Follina) in days [S1]. STEP 3: Observed template is thread-hijack email, HTML attachment, ZIP, LNK plus rundll32 DLL, then Qbot [S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued opportunistic Qbot-style loader delivery to any reachable organization. MDCOA is use of a new unpatched Office or Windows flaw against defense contractors to gain footholds later handed to ransomware operators [S1]. Candidate indicators: HTML attachments that write ZIP archives, rundll32.exe launched from LNK files, msdt-related Word child processes, and obama-tagged Qakbot configs [S1][S3][S7].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track commodity loader activity and takedown status because affiliates can re-emerge after infrastructure disruption [S5]. (2) Authorities: mitigations such as disabling the MSDT URL protocol or blocking HTML-smuggled archives are configuration actions for network owners; defensive response stays within DODIN operations authorities. (3) Mission assurance: prioritize patching and mail filtering for mission-critical enclaves, since this activity precedes ransomware [S1]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with DC3 and the DIB community for contractor mail exposure.
